query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a 10 μm thick Al2O3 ceramic coating to the surface of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance by reducing the oxidation rate by at least 50% relative to the uncoated material, at temperatures up to 1000 °C, in air, for exposure times up to 100 hours, and under tensile loading up to 500 MPa, without compromising its room- and high-temperature mechanical performance.
generation.intervention: Applying a 10 μm thick Al2O3 ceramic coating
generation.conditions: Temperature up to 1000 °C, air atmosphere, exposure time up to 100 hours, tensile loading up to 500 MPa
generation.mechanism: The Al2O3 coating acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion, reducing the oxidation rate of the underlying HfNbTaTiZr alloy
generation.predicted_outcome: Oxidation rate reduced by at least 50% relative to the uncoated material
generation.boundary: Temperature up to 1000 °C, exposure time up to 100 hours, tensile loading up to 500 MPa
generation.uncertainty: The actual oxidation rate reduction may vary depending on the coating thickness, morphology, and adherence to the substrate, as well as the specific test conditions

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the oxidation rate of the coated material is not reduced by at least 30% relative to the uncoated material, or if the tensile properties of the coated material are compromised (i.e., tensile strength or ductility reduced by more than 10%) after exposure to air at 1000 °C for 100 hours, then the hypothesis is falsified
